ctx.x: exposed to them. But shortly thereafter I asked my mother if I could go up and meet Ella B. Moore. Now, Ella B. Moore and Chinch Moore had a show they used to bring to the Cotton Palace in Waco--that was like a big festival they'd have, maybe for nineteen days...they'd have a big fair and they'd have a rodeo...but they always would have a colored show. And they had these people who worked on minstrels and worked on carnivals and worked on road shows. They always had some of them at these shows.

So I went up and I asked Ella B. Moore where she was from and she said, Dallas. Well, Dallas was 99 miles north of Waco. And she asked me my name, and she said, "You know, I'm going to call you Willie." I told her my name was Sammy. She said, "I'm going to call you Willie because I like you." And I promised her that someday I would make that big trip from Waco, you know, 99 miles north to see her. And she says, "Well, okay."
